mainTopic: When must a woman check herself for blood around relations with her husband: the limits of שיעור וסת, the cloth of צנועות, and שמואל's rule for a woman with or without a fixed וסת.
overview: This amud deals with when a woman checks herself for blood around the time she is with her husband. First, רב יהודה and then רב הונא rule that she should not do extra checks that would make a careful husband worry and stay away from her. Along the way, the גמרא shows that the tiny time window called שיעור וסת only leaves room for a quick wipe (קינוח), not a full בדיקה. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה's check before relations. רבי אמי calls it the cloth of צנועות. After pushback, רבא explains that every woman must check, and 'צנועות' means women who use a fresh cloth each time. Then the גמרא examines שמואל's rule that a woman with no fixed וסת must check before relations. רבי אבא בר ירמיה explains that a woman with a fixed וסת checks only when awake. רבא learns from this that שמואל holds no check is needed just for the husband. A ברייתא about husbands returning home seems to clash with this. The גמרא answers that the husband's request is itself the best check. The amud ends with רב פפא asking רבא whether one may rely on that ברייתא in practice.

steps.title: Should a woman check herself before being with her husband?
steps.stepSummary: ר' זירא asks רב יהודה whether a woman should do a בדיקה for blood before being with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: ר' זירא asked רב יהודה: Should a woman check herself before being with her husband?
steps.whatsHappening: ר' זירא asks a practical question: should a woman check herself for blood before being intimate with her husband?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who has a period becomes a נדה and is forbidden to her husband. The question is whether she should check beforehand as an extra safeguard, or whether no check is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (opens a question)
An internal check for blood / she should check

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked Rav Yehuda:
A woman, what is the law: should she check herself for her husband?
phrases.notes: "For her husband" means before being intimate with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman should do a בדיקה before relations with her husband.

steps.title: רב יהודה: she should not check
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that she should not check herself beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She should not check.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a short answer: no, she should not check beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a reason yet. That leaves room for ר' זירא to push back in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: She should not check

phrases.english: He said to him: She should not check.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No בדיקה should be done before relations.

steps.title: What harm would checking do?
steps.stepSummary: ר' זירא challenges the answer: why not let her check, since there seems to be no harm?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let her check. What is wrong with that?
steps.whatsHappening: ר' זירא pushes back: checking seems harmless, maybe even good, so why tell her not to?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that an extra check only adds caution. The objection forces רב יהודה to explain his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is wrong with that?

phrases.english: But let her check. What is wrong with that?

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that she should not check
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Checking adds caution and seems to cause no harm, so forbidding it needs a reason.

steps.title: Checking would make the husband anxious and keep him away
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains: if she checks, her husband will start to worry and will stay away from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, his heart will trouble him and he will stay away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives his reason: checking beforehand would make the husband nervous, and he would end up keeping away from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checks every time, the husband will think she is unsure about her status. A careful husband would then hold back from his wife out of fear. Avoiding that harm to the marriage outweighs the small benefit of checking.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart strikes him; he feels worry or doubt
He separates; stays away from his wife

steps.whatToRemember: A woman is not told to check before relations, because it would lead her husband to worry and stay away from her.

phrases.english: If so, his heart will trouble him and he will stay away.
phrases.notes: "His heart" is the husband's: he'll worry she might be a נדה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the hidden reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzMaskana: Checking has a real cost: the husband becomes anxious and separates.

steps.title: Should she check right afterward, to make the husband liable for a חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: ר' אבא asks רב הונא whether a woman should check herself within the שיעור וסת right after relations. If she finds blood, her husband would be obligated to bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ר' אבא asked רב הונא: Should a woman check herself within the time of שיעור וסת, in order to make her husband liable for a חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Should a woman check herself immediately after relations, within the very short time window called שיעור וסת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood found within that tiny window shows she was already a נדה during relations. Since the husband acted by mistake, he would owe a חטאת. The question is whether she should check in order to find this out.

keyTerms.meaning: The tiny time window right after relations, within which blood shows she was a נדה during them
To make someone liable
A sin-offering brought for an accidental sin

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba asked Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה מַהוּ שֶׁתִּבְדּוֹק עַצְמָהּ כְּשִׁיעוּר וֶסֶת,
phrases.english: A woman, what is the law: should she check herself within the time of a period's onset,
in order to make her husband liable for a sin-offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question, now about checking afterward instead of before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman should check within שיעור וסת after relations to determine whether the husband owes a חטאת.

steps.title: A full check can't be done that fast
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא challenges the premise of the question: is it even possible to do a full בדיקה within שיעור וסת?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Can you even find a case of a check done within the time of שיעור וסת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא does not answer yes or no. He attacks the question itself, saying such a check is not physically possible in that short time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes a full internal בדיקה can fit inside שיעור וסת. רב הונא says that assumption is wrong, and he backs it up with a ברייתא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you find such a case? (it doesn't happen)

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not saying "no, she shouldn't check." He is saying the case ר' אבא described can't happen at all.

phrases.english: He said to him: Can you find it,
a check within the time of a period's onset?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לִבְדִיקָה כְּשִׁיעוּר וֶסֶת
steps.kashyaTarget: The premise of ר' אבא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full internal check takes longer than שיעור וסת, so the case described cannot happen.

steps.title: The ברייתא shows how tiny שיעור וסת is
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a ברייתא: שיעור וסת is like the husband leaving and the cloth going in at the very same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: What is שיעור וסת? It is like the organ and the cloth standing at the doorway: as the organ comes out, the cloth goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא proves his point from a ברייתא. It describes שיעור וסת as an almost instant moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא pictures the husband and the checking cloth both waiting at the "doorpost." The cloth enters the instant he leaves. A time window that small leaves no room for a full internal check.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison; it is like
Literally "servant"; a polite word for the male organ
Literally "witness"; the checking cloth
Doorpost; a polite image for the entrance

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: What is the time of a period's onset?
It is like the attendant and the witness
phrases.notes: The "attendant" is the husband's organ, and the "witness" is the checking cloth.

phrases.english: that stand beside the doorpost,
as the attendant goes out, the witness comes in.

steps.raayaObject: That a full בדיקה cannot fit within שיעור וסת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא defining שיעור וסת as the cloth entering the instant the husband leaves

steps.title: The time window fits only a quick wipe, not a full check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the שיעור וסת the Sages spoke about refers to a קינוח, an outer wipe, and not a בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So: the וסת time they spoke of is for wiping, not for checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא. Only a quick outside wipe can be done inside שיעור וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full internal check takes extra time. Blood found that way might have come after relations, so it cannot prove the husband owes a חטאת. Only a quick wipe fits the window.

keyTerms.meaning: So it turns out; this shows
A quick outer wipe

steps.whatToRemember: שיעור וסת is so short that only a קינוח, not a full בדיקה, fits inside it.

phrases.english: So: the period's time that they spoke of
is for wiping, and not for checking.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שיעור וסת applies to a קינוח, not to a full בדיקה.

steps.title: The question is reworded: should she wipe?
steps.stepSummary: Since a check can't fit, the גמרא rewords ר' אבא's question: should she do a quick wipe right afterward?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the law: should she wipe?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes ר' אבא's question so it makes sense: was he really asking about wiping? This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wipe can be done within שיעור וסת, so blood found that way could make the husband liable for a חטאת. Now the question is whether she should do it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected version)
She should wipe

phrases.english: Rather, what is the law: should she wipe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the question of step 5 in light of the conclusion in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman should do a קינוח right after relations, which could make the husband liable for a חטאת.

steps.title: A second version of ר' אבא's question: checking to make the husband bring an אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: Some say ר' אבא asked something different: should a woman check herself after relations so her husband would have to bring an אשם תלוי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is what he asked him: should a woman examine herself in order to make her husband liable to bring an אשם תלוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of ר' אבא's question to רב הונא. In this version she checks after relations, not inside the שיעור וסת, and the result would be an אשם תלוי instead of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she checks a little later and finds blood, we cannot know whether it was there during relations. That doubt means the husband brings an אשם תלוי, the offering for a possible sin, and not a חטאת for a certain sin. So the question is whether she should check at all when the only result is to create such a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A provisional guilt offering, brought when someone is not sure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the same question of ר' אבא from step 5, just remembered differently.

phrases.english: Some say, this is what he asked him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is ר' אבא asking רב הונא, the same people as in step 5.

phrases.english: What is the law, should a woman examine herself
in order to make her husband liable for a provisional guilt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the question discussed in steps 5 to 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should a woman check herself after relations when the only result would be to make her husband bring an אשם תלוי?

steps.title: רב הונא answers that she should not check
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that she should not check herself for this purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: she should not examine herself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a short answer: no, she should not do this check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gives no reason yet. The reason comes two steps later, after ר' אבא pushes back.

keyTerms.meaning: She should not check

phrases.english: He said to him: She should not examine herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She should not check herself after relations for this purpose.

steps.title: Why not let her check?
steps.stepSummary: ר' אבא pushes back: what harm would a check do?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let her examine herself. What is wrong with that?
steps.whatsHappening: ר' אבא challenges רב הונא's answer by asking what could be wrong with checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking looks harmless and even helpful, since it could show the husband he needs a קרבן. So the challenge is: why stop her from doing something that gives more information?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is wrong with that?

phrases.english: And let her examine herself. What is wrong with that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that she should not check.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A check seems to cause no harm, so there is no clear reason to forbid it.

steps.title: The husband would worry and stay away
steps.stepSummary: If she checked, her husband would grow anxious and separate from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, his heart will trouble him and he will separate from her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא explains his ruling: such checks would make the husband afraid and he would keep away from his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harm is in the marriage, not in the הלכה. A careful husband who keeps hearing about possible sins would start to fear relations and would separate from her. So the extra check does more damage than good.

keyTerms.meaning: His heart strikes him: he is troubled by worry or guilt
He separates: he keeps away from his wife

steps.whatToRemember: According to this version, a woman does not check after relations just to create an אשם תלוי, because it would push her husband away from her.

phrases.english: If so,
his heart will strike him and he will separate from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the hidden reason for the ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Checking would make the husband anxious so that he separates from his wife, so she should not check.

steps.title: The cloth before relations is called the cloth of צנועות
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line about checking before relations, רבי אמי quotes רבי ינאי: this is 'the cloth of צנועות', careful women.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and at the time she is about to (have relations), etc.' רבי אמי said in the name of רבי ינאי: this is the cloth of careful women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about checking before relations. רבי אמי, quoting רבי ינאי, calls that checking cloth the cloth of צנועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling it the cloth of צנועות makes the check sound like an extra act that only especially careful women do. That sets up the next challenge, because the משנה seems to require it.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth used for checking
Careful, modest, especially pious women
Etc.: the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: 'And at the time that she is about to,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: she checks when she is about to have relations with her husband.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yannai said:
And this is the examination cloth of careful women.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁהִיא עוֹבֶרֶת וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The check before relations is called 'the cloth of צנועות'.

steps.title: The משנה says 'required', not 'careful women'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges this: the משנה says women are required to check, but you say only careful women do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל said to רבי אמי: the תנא teaches 'required', and you teach 'careful women'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל attacks רבי אמי's wording because it seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says all women must check, so the check is an obligation. Calling it the cloth of צנועות makes it sound optional. The two cannot both be true.

keyTerms.meaning: Required (the women must do it)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel said to Rabbi Ami:
The tanna teaches 'they are required,'
and you teach 'careful women'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's statement in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's description of the check as being for צנועות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the check an obligation for every woman, while 'צנועות' suggests it is only extra piety.

steps.title: Anyone who keeps the Sages' words is called צנוע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains: he did not mean the check is optional. Anyone who obeys the חכמים is called צנוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say that anyone who keeps the words of the חכמים is called 'careful'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי defends himself. 'צנועות' was praise for women who keep the required law, not a sign that the check is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees the check is required. He is simply using the word צנוע for every person who follows the חכמים, so his words and the משנה no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: One who keeps the words of the Sages
Careful, modest, pious (a person who does the right thing)

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַמְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
phrases.english: For I say that anyone who keeps the words of the Sages
is called 'careful'.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַמְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים נִקְרָא ״צָנוּעַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'צנועות' means women who do more than the law requires.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צנועות' means any woman who keeps the Sages' rules, so the check is still required.

steps.title: Someone who ignores the חכמים is a רשע, not just 'not צנוע'
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: by רבי אמי's words, a person who ignores the חכמים is only 'not צנוע', but such a person should be called a רשע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and someone who does not keep the words of the חכמים is just not called 'careful', but is not called 'wicked'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רבי אמי's answer, because it describes breaking the law too gently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If צנוע just means 'law-abiding', then the opposite of צנוע is someone who breaks the law. That person is a רשע, not merely 'not especially careful'. So the word צנוע does not fit someone who only does the basic duty.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked person
Is not called

phrases.english: Rava said:
And one who does not keep the words of the Sages:
it is only 'careful' that he is not called,
but he is not called 'wicked'?
phrases.notes: This is a question asked to make a point: of course such a person is called wicked!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים — ״צָנוּעַ״ הוּא דְּלָא מִקְּרֵי, הָא ״רָשָׁע״ לָא מִקְּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אמי's answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that anyone who keeps the Sages' words is called צנוע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opposite of a law-keeper is a רשע, so 'צנוע' is too weak a word for someone who simply obeys the law.

steps.title: רבא: צנועות never reuse a checking cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation. צנועות never reuse a cloth that was already used to check before relations. Women who are less careful reuse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: careful women, once they used a cloth to check before one act of relations, do not use it again before another act. Women who are not careful reuse it and don't mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רבי אמי's explanation and gives his own. The check itself is required for everyone; the 'careful' part is using a fresh cloth each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps both sides true. The משנה's word 'required' refers to the check itself, which every woman must do. 'צנועות' refers to an extra step: not reusing a cloth, since a used cloth is not as clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means the checking cloth (the same as עִדָּן), not 'until'
Marital relations
They don't mind / are not particular

steps.whatToRemember: The check before relations is required for every woman. Being 'צנועות' means using a fresh cloth each time.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Careful women: the cloth with which they examined themselves
phrases.notes: Don't read עַד as 'until'. Here it means the checking cloth.

phrases.english: before this act of relations,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בּוֹדְקוֹת בּוֹ לִפְנֵי תַּשְׁמִישׁ אַחֵר,
phrases.english: they do not examine with it before another act of relations;
and those who are not careful women
examine with it and do not mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אמי's answer, which step 17 rejected, with a new explanation of 'צנועות'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new meaning to the word, which settles the clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'צנועות' means anyone who keeps the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'צנועות' means women who do not reuse a checking cloth. The check itself is required for all.

steps.title: שמואל: a woman with no fixed וסת must check before relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's statement: a woman with no fixed cycle may not have relations until she checks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אבא בר ירמיה in the name of שמואל: a woman who has no fixed cycle is forbidden to have relations until she checks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement mentioned earlier and now looks at it closely. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל names one kind of woman, one without a וסת, and requires her to check before relations. Naming only her raises the question of what happens with a woman who does have a fixed cycle.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to a statement quoted earlier in order to discuss it
A fixed, predictable time when her period comes
Forbidden to have marital relations

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Zeira said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יִרְמְיָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abba bar Yirmeya said that Shmuel said:
A woman who does not have a fixed menstrual cycle
is forbidden to have relations until she examines herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צנועות discussion and returns to a statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman without a fixed וסת may not have relations until she checks.

steps.title: Does a woman with a וסת need no check at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges: does this mean a woman with a fixed cycle does not need to check? That seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אבא בר ירמיה: if she has no cycle, she needs a check; if she has a cycle, she does not need a check?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges שמואל's rule by looking at what it implies. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל only mentions a woman without a וסת, it sounds like a woman with a וסת may skip the check. But our משנה says every woman checks before relations, so this implication seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: She needs a check

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying that a woman with a וסת needs no check. He is pointing out that שמואל's words seem to say so, and asking how that can be.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abba bar Yirmeya:
If she has no fixed cycle, she needs an examination,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת — לָא בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה?
phrases.english: but if she has a fixed cycle, she does not need an examination?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת — בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה, יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת — לָא בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 19 implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule, which names only a woman without a וסת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Naming only her implies that a woman with a וסת needs no check, but the משנה requires every woman to check before relations.

steps.title: Awake versus asleep: when a woman with a fixed cycle must check
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ירמיה answers רבי זירא. A woman with a fixed וסת checks only if she is awake, not if she is asleep. A woman with no fixed וסת must check either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If she has a fixed cycle, she must check when she is awake. She does not need to check when she is asleep. If she has no fixed cycle, she must check whether she is awake or asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ירמיה answers רבי זירא's question. He explains what שמואל really meant when he singled out a woman with no fixed וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא thought שמואל's words meant a woman with a fixed וסת never needs to check. That would contradict the משנה. The answer is that she does need to check when awake, like the משנה says. The only case where she is excused is when she is asleep, and that is the difference שמואל had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, predictable menstrual cycle
Awake
Asleep
An examination to make sure she has not seen blood

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אבא בר ירמיה, answering רבי זירא's question from the previous step.

phrases.english: If she has a fixed cycle —
when awake, she needs a check;
when asleep, she does not need a check;
if she has no fixed cycle —

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עֵרָה בֵּין יְשֵׁנָה בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה.
phrases.english: whether awake or asleep, she needs a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל meant a woman with a fixed וסת never needs to check, against the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: With a fixed וסת she checks only when awake. With no fixed וסת she always checks.

steps.title: רבא suggests a different answer that could have been given
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רבי אבא בר ירמיה did not give another answer: a woman with a fixed וסת checks only if she handles טהרות, not just for her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He could have answered differently. If she has a fixed cycle, she needs a check for טהרות but not for her husband. If she has no fixed cycle, she needs a check even for her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out another way רבי זירא's question could have been answered. This sets up his conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This other answer splits the case differently. The question is not whether she is awake or asleep, but whether the check is for טהרות or only for her husband. רבא is not attacking the answer. He is getting ready to learn something from the fact that this answer was not chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure food and items that a woman handles
For her husband, meaning for relations with him

phrases.english: Rava said:
But let him say to him —
phrases.notes: He means: why didn't רבי אבא בר ירמיה answer רבי זירא this way instead?

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת, לִטְהָרוֹת בָּעֲיָא בְּדִיקָה,
phrases.english: if she has a fixed cycle, for pure items she needs a check,
for her husband she does not need a check;
if she has no fixed cycle,
even for her husband she also needs a check.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different possible answer to step 20 than the one given in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why didn't רבי אבא בר ירמיה split the case by טהרות versus husband?

steps.title: שמואל holds no check is needed just for the husband
steps.stepSummary: Since that other answer was not given, רבא learns that שמואל holds a check is never needed just for relations with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he did not answer that way, we learn that שמואל holds: whenever it is only for her husband, no check is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion from the fact that the other answer was not given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל had required a check for the husband in any case, the answer from step 22 would have worked nicely. Since it was not used, שמואל must hold that a check is never needed just for the husband. That is why רבי אבא בר ירמיה had to split the case by awake versus asleep instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this: a conclusion drawn from what was said or not said
He holds

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, שמואל holds that a check is not required just for relations with her husband.

phrases.english: And since he did not say it to him this way,
learn from it that Shmuel holds:
whenever it is for her husband, she does not need a check.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָכִי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from step 22's suggested answer not being used
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view on checking for the husband
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of רבי אבא בר ירמיה, who did not give the answer based on טהרות
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא concludes that, according to שמואל, a check that is only for relations with her husband is not required.

steps.title: Husbands returning home may be with their wives without a check
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: men coming home from a trip, a house of mourning, or a celebration may be with their wives, asleep or awake. This applies only if they left them pure. If they left them impure, she stays impure until she says she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Donkey drivers and laborers, and those coming from a house of mourning or a house of feasting: their wives are presumed pure for them. They may come and be with them, whether the wives are asleep or awake. When is this said? When they left them presumed pure. But if they left them presumed impure, she is always impure until she tells him, 'I am pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about men returning home. It says their wives keep their pure status, so no check is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'whether asleep or awake.' So even an awake wife does not need to check. That point matters for the next step. The status the husband left her with stays in place until something changes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey drivers, who travel away from home
Laborers
A house of mourning
A house of feasting, such as a wedding
A presumed status of purity
When is this said? It limits the ruling to a certain case

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Donkey drivers and laborers,
and those coming from a house of mourning or a house of feasting —
their wives are, for them, presumed pure,
and they may come and stay with them,
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying they may have relations with them.

phrases.english: whether they are asleep or awake.
When is this said?
When they left them presumed pure,
but if they left them presumed impure —
she is always impure,
until she says to him, 'I am pure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about checking before relations, which will be tested against שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wives left pure stay presumed pure, and the husband may be with them without a check, whether they are asleep or awake. Wives left impure stay impure until they say they are pure.

steps.title: How does שמואל fit this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows relations without a check even when the wife is awake. In רבי אבא בר ירמיה's version, שמואל would require a check in that case whether she has a fixed וסת or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how would שמואל explain this ברייתא? If it is about a woman with a fixed cycle, the 'awake' case is difficult. If it is about a woman with no fixed cycle, both the awake and asleep cases are difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא בר ירמיה's version of שמואל using the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, a woman with a fixed וסת must check when awake. A woman with no fixed וסת must always check. The ברייתא says no check is needed, asleep or awake. Neither kind of woman fits, so the ברייתא seems to contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets up or explains: which case the source is talking about
It is difficult; there is a problem

phrases.english: But how would שמואל set this up?
phrases.notes: He means: what kind of woman would שמואל say the ברייתא is talking about?

phrases.aramaic: אִי בְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת — קַשְׁיָא עֵרָה,
phrases.english: If it is about one who has a fixed cycle — 'awake' is difficult,
and if it is about one who has no fixed cycle —
both 'awake' and 'asleep' are difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 24 to challenge the explanation in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא בר ירמיה's explanation of שמואל (step 21)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets an awake wife skip the check. Step 21 requires a check from an awake wife, whether or not she has a fixed וסת. So the ברייתא fits neither case.

steps.title: The husband's request counts as the best check
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a woman with a fixed וסת. When her husband asks her for relations, that request is itself the best possible check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the ברייתא is talking about a woman who has a fixed וסת. Since her husband asked her for relations, there is no better check than that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 25. It explains that the ברייתא's case does include a kind of check, so it does not argue with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the ברייתא allows relations with an awake wife without a בדיקה. The answer is that the woman has a fixed וסת, and the husband's request makes her stop and think whether she is pure. If she had felt anything she would tell him, so his asking works like a בדיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeps the original reading and explains it differently)
He asked her (for relations)
A check that she is pure

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say that no check is needed. It says the husband's request is itself a check, and an even better one than an ordinary בדיקה.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where she has a fixed cycle,
phrases.notes: This is about the ברייתא from step 24, where the husbands come home from a trip.

phrases.english: and since he asked her for relations,
you have no greater check than this.
phrases.notes: When he asks, she thinks it over. If she had sensed her period, she would remember and tell him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: a fixed וסת, and the husband's request counts as a check.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows relations with an awake wife without any check, against שמואל as רבי אבא בר ירמיה reports him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא deals with a fixed וסת, and the request works as a check, so it fits שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a בדיקה does not have to be a physical exam. In this case, the woman thinking it over when asked counts as a check.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about acting on this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא whether one may actually act according to this ברייתא in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: What is the הלכה about acting according to this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks רבא a practical question: may people rely on this ברייתא? This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has now been explained so that it fits שמואל. רב פפא wants to know if it is the actual practice, since it allows relations even when she is asleep and cannot be asked. Maybe she must be woken and asked first.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?
To act (in practice)
A ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
What is the law about acting like this baraita?
phrases.notes: He means in real life: can a husband rely on it, even when his wife is asleep?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא מַהוּ לְמֶעְבַּד כִּי הָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is explained, רב פפא asks whether it is the practical halacha.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband may rely on the ברייתא in practice and be with his wife without a check, even while she sleeps.
